title: LED-matrix frame-sync row shows LOCK during LOS
description: _matrix_status() sends self.sync.state unconditionally. FrameSynchronizer changes state only when octets arrive (framesync.py _step). After the last CADU of a pass it stays LOCK (or FLYWHEEL) indefinitely; checked: state 'LOCK' after 3 CADUs and still 'LOCK' after a later feed with no data. The M line keeps sending 'L', so row 1 (frame sync LOCK) stays fully lit during LOS. Every other link row is gated on reception within the LOS timeout.
failure_scenario: The pass ends and the LOS timeout expires. Row 0 (AOS) goes dark and rows 3-5 blank, but row 1 stays lit as 'frame sync LOCK' for hours until the next pass. The matrix contradicts itself and reports a lock with no signal.
proposed_fix: In _matrix_status, send sync None or 'SEARCH' when self.rx.los is true (or when no frame arrived within los_timeout_s), e.g. "sync": "PACKET" if packet_mode else (None if rx.los else self.sync.state).
verifier_fix_notes: In _matrix_status, gate on reception: "sync": "PACKET" if packet_mode else ("SEARCH" if rx.los or not recent else self.sync.state). Sending 'SEARCH' rather than None keeps the field 'known: no lock'. Optionally apply the same gating to the snapshot's sync.state, or call self.sync._lose_lock() on the AOS->LOS transition (that also counts a lock loss, so prefer display gating). Add a test: CADUs, then a time past the LOS timeout, then matrix_line() must not carry 'L'.

title: Radio panels say "[gds] rcu = false" when rcu is true but the RCU path is unavailable
description: _register_check() returns 'not read back: no Radio Control Unit ([gds] rcu = false) ...' whenever radio_mgr or radio_mgr.rcu is None. The same false attribution appears in dashboard.html:1541 ('off ([gds] rcu = false): ...') and 1505 ('needs the Radio Control Unit, [gds] rcu = false') whenever radio.rcu is false. With [gds] rcu = true that also happens when the Router Bridge is unavailable (gds.py:2609-2617, link None, so no _Rcu) or the E22 serial port did not open (radio None, so mgr None, gds.py:2645-2650).
failure_scenario: Checked: cfg['gds']['rcu'] = True, then attach_radio(None, None, 'serial port: ENOENT'). The snapshot gives radio.rcu False and register_check 'not read back: no Radio Control Unit ([gds] rcu = false) ...', while station_io.rcu_configured is True. The operator is sent to station.toml, which is already correct, instead of to the missing bridge package or USB-UART.
proposed_fix: Branch on cfg['gds']['rcu'] when there is no rcu path: rcu = false keeps the current text; rcu = true reports 'configured ([gds] rcu = true) but not available: no Router Bridge / radio serial port not open'. Mirror this in dashboard.html 1505 and 1541 (e.g. from station_io.rcu_configured) and in docs/13:1092-1093.
verifier_fix_notes: In _register_check, when rm or rm.rcu is None: if not cfg['gds']['rcu'], keep the current text; otherwise return 'not read back: [gds] rcu = true but the Radio Control Unit is not available (' + (self.radio_unavailable or 'no Router Bridge') + ')'. In dashboard.html 1505 and 1541, choose the wording from S.station_io.rcu_configured: 'configured but not available' versus 'off ([gds] rcu = false)'. Update docs/13 to match, and add a test_web case with rcu = true and no backend.

title: D-77 fault_log default never reaches upgraded stations: 3.0 station.toml carries an explicit fault_log = false
description: The 3.0 shipped station.toml contained 'fault_log = false' as a mirrored default (removed in this diff). The App copies station.toml to data/ once, and README 2.6 tells the operator to restore the old data/ folder on update. merge() applies fault_log_default() only when the key is absent, so every station upgraded from 3.0 keeps fault_log false. Selecting model = "E22-400T37S" then leaves the T37S abnormal-status log off (the configuration tool --write and the GDS volatile writes clear REG1 b2), with no hint.
failure_scenario: A 3.0 station is updated to 3.1 by the README procedure and switched to the T37S. regs_from_cfg() writes REG1 b2 = 0, so the module's under-voltage and over-temperature reports never appear, contrary to D-77 ('fault_log defaults to true when model = E22-400T37S').
proposed_fix: Note in the 3.1 upgrade text (README 2.6 / CHANGELOG): delete the old 'fault_log = false' line. Optionally log an INFO at start when model is E22-400T37S and fault_log is explicitly false: 'T37S abnormal-status log off by station.toml'.
verifier_fix_notes: Add a 3.1 upgrade note (CHANGELOG and README 2.6): 'delete the line fault_log = false from a station.toml copied from 3.0 (it was the old mirrored default; D-77 now derives it from [radio] model)'. Optionally log an INFO at start when model = E22-400T37S and fault_log is explicitly false: 'T37S abnormal-status log off by station.toml'. No code change is required.

title: Station harness checks claim more than they test (4 Hz redraw, millis() wrap)
description: 'loop() redraws the matrix at 4 Hz' requires only >= 2 draws in 600 ms, so it also passes for a redraw on every loop pass or at ~3.4 Hz. 'the RCU age grows across hellos (re-anchored, never wraps with millis())' (line 181) only moves g_rcu_t_ms back by 7 s and 3 s; no millis() wrap is exercised.
failure_scenario: A regression that sets kMxPeriodMs to 0 (redraw every pass) still passes 'at 4 Hz'. A signed or overflowing age computation across the 2^32 ms wrap would not be caught by the 'never wraps' check.
proposed_fix: Count draws over a fixed window and require 2-3 per 600 ms (or check the interval between draws equals kMxPeriodMs). For the wrap, set g_rcu_t_ms = millis() + 0xFFFFF000u - 0xFFFFFFFFu (an anchor just before a wrap) and check that the age stays within the expected small value. Or rename the checks to what they test.
verifier_fix_notes: Check the redraw interval exactly. Record the draw times inside run_loop() (or count draws in a 1 s window) and require the gaps to equal kMxPeriodMs within a few ms (e.g. 3-5 draws per 1 s), not just a lower bound. For the RCU age: make the wrap crossing explicit and independent of start-up time. Set g_rcu_t_ms = (uint32_t)millis() - 7000u and comment that it crosses 2^32 when millis() < 7000. Add a long-age case: call rcu_age_s() repeatedly after moving the anchor back 0x7FFF0000 ms twice, and check the age keeps growing past 4294967 s (49.7 days) and saturates at 0x7FFFFFFF. Or rename the check to what it tests.

title: Nicla recovery (EVR 0x0607) is not parsed: after a transient loss the ground shows the Nicla LOST for good and drops the 'not separated' YELLOW alarm
description: The flight never re-probes the Nicla after a run-time loss. NiclaAru::ok_ is only set in begin(), so reprobe_instruments() never calls probe_nicla() again and no new 0x060B is sent. Recovery is reported only as INFO 0x0607 "Nicla Sense ME responding again" (flight.cpp:1998), which names no bus. dictionary.evr_instrument_bus() and evr_instrument_lost() (dictionary.py:166/194) and SensorBusState.on_evr() ignore 0x0607. The Nicla's report therefore stays 'lost' (from 0x0606), and separation() counts only state == 'acquired' (sensors.py:357). tests/test_sensors.py:225 'recovers' the Nicla with an 0x060B that the flight cannot produce, so the test passes on a path that does not exist. The same stale-LOST display happens when a routine INFO 0x060B for a re-acquired RM3100 is dropped by the EVR gate or the EVRLEVEL filter.
failure_scenario: Owner layout with the Nicla and RM3100 outboard both on A4/A5. At boot: 0x060B x2 plus 0x060D 'not separated', so separated=False and the YELLOW alarm 'sensor wiring: RM3100 and Nicla not on separate buses' is up. docs/08 T-FD-04: unplug the Nicla for 10 s, giving 0x0606, then reconnect, giving 0x0607, and HK NICLA_ME is OK again. Reproduced with SensorBusState: snapshot(0x07FF) -> separated None, 'unknown (no current acquisition report of the Nicla Sense ME)', lost=['Nicla Sense ME (A4/A5)'], nicla.state 'lost' with hk_ok True. The YELLOW wiring alarm is gone although the wiring is unchanged, and the SPACECRAFT tab shows the Nicla red LOST until the next reboot.
proposed_fix: Flight: print the bus in 0x0607 ("Nicla Sense ME responding again on %s") and add it to SENSOR_BUS_EVRS. In SensorBusState.on_evr, treat 0x0607 as an acquisition of the Nicla on that bus (or on its last bus). As a fallback in snapshot()/separation(), count a 'lost' instrument as acquired when the newest HK has its bit set and that HK is newer than the loss report. Replace the 0x060B Nicla 'recovery' in test_sensors.py:225 with the real 0x0607 sequence.
verifier_fix_notes: Flight: print the bus in 0x0607 ("Nicla Sense ME responding again on %s", aru_bus_), add it to SENSOR_BUS_EVRS, and re-run report_separation(u) for both units on recovery so a shared bus WARNs again. Ground: add EVR_NICLA_RECOVERED = 0x0607 to evr_instrument_bus() (or handle it in on_evr) as an 'acquired' report on the named bus, falling back to the last known bus for the old text. Optional robustness: in separation(), count a 'lost' instrument as acquired when the newest HK has its bit set and that HK is newer than the loss report. Replace the 0x060B recovery in test_sensors.py:225 with the real 0x0606 -> 0x0607 sequence and assert separated returns to False in the shared-bus layout. Add a cross-check test that every flight EVR naming the Nicla or an RM3100 recovery is in SENSOR_BUS_EVRS.

title: Simulator sets IMU_F_STATS even when imu_nwin is 0 (the flight never does)
description: IMU_FLAGS_SIM = 0x47 (sim.py:125) is always sent, but _imu_stats() returns {'imu_nwin': 0} with sentinel statistics when no whole SCLK second has passed since the previous ATT (sim.py:1238). The flight sets IMU_F_STATS only when windows() != 0 (flight.cpp:1863). The ground copes (sensors.py:242 checks both), but the simulator, which the dashboard tests and docs examples rely on, breaks the ATT v4 invariant 'STATS <=> imu_nwin >= 1'.
failure_scenario: Two simulated ATTs in the same SCLK second (or the first ATT at SCLK < 1 s) give imu_flags with STATS set and imu_nwin 0, a state the real spacecraft cannot send.
proposed_fix: In _att(), clear bit 0x02 from imu_flags when the stats dict has imu_nwin == 0.
verifier_fix_notes: In _att(): after v.update(self._imu_stats(t)), `if not v.get('imu_nwin'): v['imu_flags'] &= ~0x02` (use a named IMU_F_STATS constant from the dictionary bit list). Add a simulator test asserting STATS iff imu_nwin >= 1.

title: ImuStats only resets in gen_att(): the first ATT after SAFE/BOOT aggregates every window since boot and reports imu_nwin = 255 (saturated)
description: imu_stats_.add() runs at every 1 Hz sample in every mode (start_mag_sample), but imu_stats_.reset() is only called in gen_att() (flight.cpp:1869). ATT is off in BOOT and SAFE (kModeCadence datalink.cpp:277-278), and the spacecraft boots into SAFE and waits for the ground. ImuStats::windows() saturates at 255 (attitude.h:104) while n_ keeps counting, so the first ATT after the operator commands CRUISE/TEST has these values over the whole SAFE time (hours): vib_rms (RMS of all windows), the peaks (max over hours) and rate_mean. imu_nwin is 255 with no saturation marker. The ground presents these as 'window statistics over the ATT period' (docs/13 9.4; dashboard.html:2074 'Windows aggregated 255'), and gds.ImuHistory plots them as one point at that ATT's receive time. The motion state is 'moving' if anything moved at any time in SAFE.
failure_scenario: Boot, 2 h in SAFE (about 7200 windows read), then CRUISE. The first ATT (generated at once because last_gen_s_ is 0) has imu_nwin=255 instead of 60, rate_peak and vib_peak equal to the largest values seen during the 2 h, and rate_mean equal to the 2 h mean. The SCIENCE table shows 'Windows aggregated 255' and possibly 'moving'. The IMU chart point at that time stands for 2 h, not one ATT period.
proposed_fix: Reset imu_stats_ whenever ATT is not being generated: in tick_1hz, when the ATT period in force is 0, call imu_stats_.reset() (it keeps last_win_). Or cap the aggregation to the nominal ATT period, e.g. reset at set_mode(). On the ground, render imu_nwin == 255 as '>= 255 (saturated)'.
verifier_fix_notes: Flight: in tick_1hz, after periods_in_force(per), call imu_stats_.reset() whenever the ATT period in force is 0 or the spacecraft is hibernating. reset() keeps last_win_, so de-duplication survives. The first ATT after the mode change then covers at most the last second, or 0 windows with STATS clear, which the ground already handles. Mirror this in sim.py (set imu_win_end = int(t) while ATT is off). Ground: render imu_nwin == 255 as '>= 255 (saturated)'. Document in docs/05 and docs/13 that the first ATT after a mode change covers only the time since ATT generation started.

title: docs/15 still documents the old (VENTUNO) station pin plan and old defaults: RCU AUX D4, lamps D5/D6/D7, buzzer A0, SX NRST A1, archive_max_gb 16, fault_log false
description: The code (sketch.ino:149/152/532, pin plan H, D-72) uses RCU M0/M1/AUX = D2/D3/D7, lamps AOS/ALARM/UPLINK = D4/D5/D6, buzzer A1, SX126x NRST A4. docs/15 contradicts this in: section 5 heading 'Station sketch build settings (VENTUNO Q MCU)' (line 430); line 437 'RCU on D2 M0, D3 M1, D4 AUX'; line 441 'PIN_SX_NRST ... A1'; line 444 'PIN_RCU_AUX D4'; line 445 'D5, D6, D7, A0'; and line 406 ([gds] rcu 'M0/M1/AUX on D2/D3/D4'). It also contradicts config.py: line 410 archive_max_gb default 16.0 (code 8.0, D-80) and line 277 fault_log default 'false' (code: true for model = E22-400T37S, fault_log_default(), D-77). docs/13:2997 also still says 'default 16 GB'. tests/test_docs.py does not check these values.
failure_scenario: An operator wires the station from docs/15. The E22 AUX output goes to D4, which the sketch drives as the AOS lamp output: two outputs fight on one net, the RCU never sees AUX and reports FAILED. The SX126x NRST lands on A1, the buzzer driver, so the radio is reset by every buzzer tone. A T37S user reads that the abnormal-status log is off by default when it is on.
proposed_fix: Update docs/15: section 5 title to the ground UNO Q; the PIN_RCU_* row to D2/D3/D7; the PIN_LED_*/PIN_BUZZER row to D4/D5/D6/A1; PIN_SX_NRST to A4; the [gds] rcu text to D2/D3/D7; archive_max_gb default to 8.0 (D-80); fault_log default to 'model-dependent: true for E22-400T37S, else false'. Fix docs/13:2997 to 8 GB. Add a docs test that reads these rows from sketch.ino and config.DEFAULTS.
verifier_fix_notes: docs/15: section 5 title -> ground UNO Q MCU; DSSQ_RADIO_SX126X text and PIN_RCU_* -> D2/D3/D7; PIN_LED_*/PIN_BUZZER -> D4/D5/D6/A1; PIN_SX_NRST -> A4 (RXEN/TXEN A2/A3 unchanged); [gds] rcu -> D2/D3/D7; archive_max_gb -> 8.0 (D-80); fault_log -> 'model-dependent: true for model = "E22-400T37S", else false (D-77)'. docs/13:2997 -> 8 GB. Same pin fix in docs/03 ground-station tables and diagrams (lines ~514, 570, 603, 671). Add a docs test that parses the PIN_* constants from sketch.ino and config.DEFAULTS and checks them against the docs/15 rows.

title: IMU_F_ cross-check only checks bit contiguity, not that flight names map to IMU_FLAG_BITS positions
description: The loop takes only the sorted VALUES of the IMU_F_ enum and asserts that they are [1<<i for i in range(len(names))]. The names are never compared, so the flight ImuFlag order is not checked against dictionary.IMU_FLAG_BITS. Contrast SENSOR_BITS/FDIR_BITS two lines above, which compare names sorted by value. The integration vector (imu_flags == 0x67) and test_bit_and_bist_decoders check numbers or the dictionary alone, so a swapped pair (e.g. IMU_F_PAIRED = 0x02 and IMU_F_STATS = 0x04 in tlm_packets.h) passes every test while the dashboard labels the bits wrongly. The same gap exists for the MAG_F_/ATT_F_/ENV_F_/RF_F_ entries the new one was added to.
failure_scenario: Edit tlm_packets.h: IMU_F_STATS = 0x04, IMU_F_PAIRED = 0x02. test_flight_header_constants_match_dictionary still passes. On the ground, a period with windows but no pairing shows the badge 'PAIRED' and 'imu_nwin 0' handling uses the wrong bit.
proposed_fix: For each prefix: e = _enum(tlm, rf"\b{prefix}(\w+)\s*=\s*(0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+)"); assert [n for n, _ in sorted(e.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])] == names and sorted(e.values()) == [1 << i for i in range(len(names))].
verifier_fix_notes: Compare names in order for IMU_F_, MAG_F_ and RF_F_: `e = _enum(tlm, rf"\b{prefix}(\w+)\s*=\s*(0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+)"); assert [n for n, _ in sorted(e.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])] == names`, keeping the contiguity assert. For ATT_F_ and ENV_F_, give an explicit alias map in the test ({'ACC': 'ACCEL', 'MAG': 'BMM150'}, {'PRESSURE': 'BARO', 'TH': 'TEMP_RH'}) and compare through it, or rename one side.

title: ImuStats: an ARU restart is not flagged as IMU_F_GAP when the pre-first-window page is read
description: The guard for 'the ARU before its first window' (win_seq 0, n 0, no STATS/MISSED) sets last_win_ = 0 and returns before the gap check, whether or not a window was already seen. After a Nicla reset (watchdog, brownout, re-plug) the flight reads a page with win_seq 0 / n 0 within the first second. The next window, win_seq 1, is then 'consecutive'. The seconds of the outage are never marked as a gap, contrary to the header comment ('a counter that moved backwards - an ARU restart - also shows as a gap'). Related doc slip: nicla_sense_me_aru.ino:58 and attitude.h:75 say 'win_seq 0 = none completed yet', but the counter wraps 255 -> 0 every 256 s.
failure_scenario: Host check (compiled into the scratch directory): add windows 130..137, reset(), then add(win_seq 0, n 0, flags 0) and add(win_seq 1, n 25, STATS). Result: gap()=0, windows()=1. The ATT says no windows were missed although the ARU was down for several seconds.
proposed_fix: In the guard, set gap_ = true when seen_ && last_win_ != 0 (the counter went back to the pre-window state), or keep the gap check before the guard. Fix the '0 = none completed yet' comments to say that win_seq 0 also follows 255.
verifier_fix_notes: In the guard: `if (seen_ && last_win_ != 0) gap_ = true;` before `last_win_ = 0`. The ARU went back to its pre-window state, i.e. it restarted. The first-ever reading (seen_ false) stays gap-free. Reword the comments: 'win_seq 0 with n 0 and no STATS/MISSED = no window completed since the ARU started; win_seq also reaches 0 after 255'. Add the host test sequence above.

title: IMU_F_PAIRED also requires a valid 9-DOF quaternion, so the ground's linear acceleration is withheld with a false reason
description: The flight sets IMU_F_PAIRED only when page-2 seq == page-0 seq AND aru_last_.motion_flags b0 (rotation vector valid). The ground gates the linear acceleration (acc - 1 g x u, which needs only q_grv and the page-0 accelerometer) on PAIRED. When q_fus is invalid but acc and q_grv come from the same rebuild, sensors.py:224 reports 'IMU_F_PAIRED clear: acc and q_grv not from one ARU rebuild', which is false. The tlm_packets.h comment and docs/05 define PAIRED purely as 'same ARU rebuild'.
failure_scenario: The 9-DOF rotation vector goes stale or fails the norm gate (ATT b0 QUAT clear) while GRV and the accelerometer are valid and paired by seq. The SCIENCE row shows 'n/a (IMU_F_PAIRED clear: acc and q_grv not from one ARU rebuild)' although they are from one rebuild, and the linear acceleration is not shown.
proposed_fix: Set IMU_F_PAIRED from aru_imu_paired_ && aru_valid_ alone; the ground already checks ATT b0 QUAT separately for the heading offset (sensors.py:226) and b1 ACCEL for the linear acceleration.
verifier_fix_notes: Set IMU_F_PAIRED from `aru_imu_paired_ && aru_valid_` (drop the motion_flags b0 term), keeping it inside the GRV-valid branch. The ground already gates the heading offset on ATT b0 QUAT and lin_acc on ATT b1 ACCEL. Add a flight host or vector case with QUAT clear and PAIRED set, and a ground test that lin_acc is produced and na.pair says 'ATT b0 QUAT clear'.

title: The displayed 'noise floor est.' for |omega| of the MEAN rate is the single-sample floor, too large by sqrt(25 x imu_nwin)
description: RATE_FLOOR_DPS = 0.07 x sqrt(3) = 0.121 deg/s is the noise magnitude of ONE gyro sample. ATT rate_mean is the mean of the window means, i.e. of about 25 x imu_nwin samples, whose white-noise floor is 0.121 / sqrt(25 x nwin), about 0.0086 deg/s at nwin 8. dashboard.html:2077 prints '|omega| of the mean rate ... (noise floor est. 0.12 deg/s)' next to that mean, and the spin-axis gate is 10 x this per-sample figure. The number shown is not the floor of the quantity it is attached to. vib_floor is correct, because vib_rms is a per-sample RMS.
failure_scenario: TEST mode, still spacecraft, imu_nwin 8. The table shows '|omega| 0.03 deg/s (noise floor est. 0.12 deg/s)', which suggests the reading is buried in noise, while the white-noise floor of that 200-sample mean is about 0.009 deg/s (the limit is the unspecified residual offset, not noise).
proposed_fix: Report the floor of the mean, RATE_FLOOR_DPS / sqrt(25 * nwin), labelled 'white-noise floor of the mean (residual offset not included)'. Or label 0.12 deg/s as 'per-sample noise (peak rate)' and move it to the Peak |rate| row.
verifier_fix_notes: Move the 0.12 deg/s per-sample figure to the 'Peak |rate|' row, labelled 'per-sample noise est. (ODR 200 Hz figure, 25 Hz not specified)'. For the mean rate, show 'white-noise floor of the mean ~ 0.007*sqrt(3/(2*nwin)) deg/s (datasheet noise density); residual offset not specified, dominates', or show no floor. If the spin-axis gate stays at 1.2 deg/s, describe it as a conservative design threshold (D-75), not '10 x the noise floor'. Update docs/13 9.4 in step.

title: docs/05 lists only the first format of EVR 0x060D: the 'not separated' WARN that drives a YELLOW alarm is undocumented
description: evrs() keeps one row per id (rows.setdefault). The flight prints two formats under 0x060D (flight.cpp:538 wrong bus, :552 'not separated'), and dictionary.SENSOR_BUS_EVRS lists both. docs/05:623 shows only '%s found on %s; the recommended bus is %s (docs/03)'.
failure_scenario: An operator who sees 'Nicla Sense ME and RM3100 outboard both on A4/A5: not separated (docs/03)' and the YELLOW alarm looks up 0x060D in docs/05 and finds only the wrong-bus text.
proposed_fix: Collect a list of formats per id and print each one (one row per distinct format), then regenerate docs/05.
verifier_fix_notes:
Collect a list of (severity, format) per id, deduplicated in order, and print one row per distinct format (or join them with '
' in one row). Regenerate docs/05. Check that the docs drift test still compares against the generator output.

title: Station Bridge ICD (docs/04 9.7, docs/06 5) still shows the 3-field hello and no M line, under a 'VENTUNO Q' heading
description: The code sends 'H|<fw>|<rcu -1/0/1>|<kb>|<rcu age s>' (sketch.ino:1704; frontpanel.parse_hello). The rcu field is the result of the last rcu_mode() call, not 'RCU present'. The GDS also sends 'M|sync|tx|rssi|margin|lost|clock' on fp_line. docs/04:897-901 documents fp_line as S/Q only and the hello as "H|<fw>|<rcu>|<kb>"; docs/06:204 says "H|<fw>|<rcu 0/1>|<kb 0/1>" = 'RCU present'. Both sections still say VENTUNO Q. These files are outside the three named docs but are the interface definition of the station link (the docs phase may still be pending).
failure_scenario: Someone writes a replacement station sketch or a test tool from docs/04. They send a 3-field hello (accepted, but the RCU state stays 'unknown') and do not implement the M line, so the LED matrix stays blank.
proposed_fix: Update docs/04 9.7 and docs/06 5 to the 4-field hello (rcu -1 never / 0 failed / 1 OK, age in s, -1 never) and to the M line with its field grammar (L/F/S/P, 0/1, dBm | '-' | 'O', [N]dB, lost, 0/1, '?' = unknown), and rename the headings to the ground UNO Q.
verifier_fix_notes: docs/04 9.7 and docs/06 5: rename to the ground UNO Q. Document the hello as 'H|<fw>|<rcu -1 never/0 failed/1 OK: last rcu_mode result>|<kb 0/1>|<rcu age s, -1 never>' (D-78), and add the M line with its field grammar exactly as in frontpanel.matrix_line() and the sketch's parse_matrix_line(). Add a docs drift test that checks the hello format string and the M field count from sketch.ino.

title: Signal power, C/N0 and Eb/N0 still get numbers at NOISE_FLOOR, where D-76 says the signal cannot be measured
description: snapshot() computes pr = signal_power_dbm(rssi, noise_pair) at line 880 without checking the margin state. The E22 C/N0 (line 887) and Eb/N0 (line 890) are built on pr. margin_assessment() at line 893 rules that for R - N < 3 dB the signal is below the noise and nothing derived from the RSSI is measurable. Even so, rx.rf.pr_est_dbm, cn0_est_dbhz and ebn0_est_db get a number whenever 0 < R - N < 3 dB. The RECEIVER 'RF now' rows (dashboard.html RF_KEYS 1330-1332) show them, and /metrics exports them as dssq_rf_pr_est_dbm, dssq_rf_cn0_est_dbhz and dssq_rf_ebn0_est_db. With the E22's 1 dB steps these values are quantisation artefacts that look like a strong link.
failure_scenario: E22 at the edge of range (the project's design case). Noise register -118 dBm, packet RSSI -117 dBm. I reproduced this in review31/LS/noisefloor.py: margin_state NOISE_FLOOR and margin_worst_est_db None, as intended. But pr_est_dbm = -123.9 dBm, cn0_est_dbhz = 45.1 dB-Hz and ebn0_est_db = +11.3 dB are shown and exported. With R - N = 2 dB, Eb/N0 reads +14.8 dB. The LoRa limit is about 6 dB, so an operator reads a healthy link while the margin row says 'not measurable'.
proposed_fix: Compute ma first. Then set pr = signal_power_dbm(rssi, noise_pair) if ma['state'] in ('SIGNAL', 'NEAR_NOISE') else None, so the E22 cn0 and ebn0 become None too. In docs/13 4.2, change the 'Signal power est.' card to say '—' when RSSI - noise < 3 dB (NOISE_FLOOR).
verifier_fix_notes: In snapshot(), compute ma first (move line 893 above 880). Then set pr = signal_power_dbm(rssi, noise_pair) if ma['state'] in ('SIGNAL', 'NEAR_NOISE') else None. The E22 cn0 and ebn0 then become None automatically. The SX126x cn0, built from the measured SNR, stays. In docs/13 4.2 (Signal power est., C/N0, Eb/N0), change the condition to: '—' when RSSI - noise < 3 dB (NOISE_FLOOR) or a value is missing. Add a test in tests/test_link_legitimacy.py that asserts pr/cn0/ebn0 are None at R-N = 1 dB on the E22.

title: During LOS, /metrics still exports the last pass's noise floor and N0 as current gauges
description: LIVE_RF_KEYS keeps last-reception values out of LOS exports. The E22 noise is queried only after a received frame (gds._module_answering docstring). So during LOS, rf.noise_dbm and rf.n0_est_dbm_hz are the last pass's values, frozen, but they are not in the set. Neither are budget.uplink.measured_* from the last RF packet.
failure_scenario: Hours into LOS, dssq_rf_noise_dbm and dssq_rf_n0_est_dbm_hz keep the last pass's values as a flat line. A noise-floor dashboard or alert sees a steady floor while nothing is being measured.
proposed_fix: Add 'noise_dbm' and 'n0_est_dbm_hz' to LIVE_RF_KEYS (keep noise_age_s). Skip budget_uplink measured_* during LOS. Update docs/13 section 16.
verifier_fix_notes: Add 'noise_dbm' and 'n0_est_dbm_hz' to LIVE_RF_KEYS, or better, skip them whenever noise_age_s > pair_s, which also covers the early AOS period. Apply the LOS skip to the budget_uplink measured_* keys. Update docs/13 section 16 accordingly.

title: Recommended margin alert never fires at the noise floor or during LOS
description: Section 16 recommends the alert 'dssq_rf_margin_worst_est_db < 3'. At NOISE_FLOOR margin_worst_est_db is None, and during LOS it is in LIVE_RF_KEYS, so the gauge is absent either way. A Prometheus comparison on an absent series does not fire. No numeric gauge for margin_state exists.
failure_scenario: The link fades into the noise: the margin goes from 4 dB to 'not measurable'. The gauge disappears and the recommended alert clears instead of firing, at the moment the link is most at risk.
proposed_fix: Export a numeric margin state (for example dssq_rf_margin_state_code). Document an alert such as 'dssq_rf_margin_worst_est_db < 3 or dssq_rf_margin_worst_max_db < 3 or absent(dssq_rf_margin_worst_est_db) and dssq_los == 0'.
verifier_fix_notes: Export the coloured margin under one name for both radios, for example dssq_rf_margin_colour_db = rxstats.margin_colour_db(). Also export a numeric dssq_rf_margin_state_code (0 SIGNAL, 1 NEAR_NOISE, 2 NOISE_FLOOR, 3 NOISE_UNKNOWN). Document alerts such as 'dssq_rf_margin_colour_db < 3', 'dssq_rf_margin_state_code == 2 and dssq_los == 0' and 'dssq_rf_margin_worst_max_db < 3' in docs/13 section 16.

title: Rate-window test will start failing on 2027-01-15
description: _rx() builds ReceiverStats with t0 = the real time.time(). The test feeds T0 = 1.8e9 (2027-01-15T08:00Z) as 'now'. _rates() uses span = max(1, min(win, now - t0)). After that date now - t0 is negative, so span = 1 s and frames_per_min becomes 360 instead of 6*60/692.5.
failure_scenario: I reproduced it by setting time.time to T0 + 30 days before construction (review31/LS/future_rates.py): frames_per_min = 360.0 against the expected 0.5199. The assertion at line 245 fails on every CI run from mid-January 2027.
proposed_fix: Set r.t0 = T0 - 1 after _rx() in this test, or monkeypatch time.time to T0 while building it.
verifier_fix_notes: In the test, set r.t0 = T0 - 1e6 (or any time well before T0) right after r = _rx(). Better, have _rx() set r.t0 = T0 - 1e6 for all tests in the file, or give ReceiverStats an optional t0 argument. Other test files use the same T0 (test_docs, test_end_to_end, test_imu_chart); check them for the same pattern.

title: (Outside the LS lens) docs/15 station-sketch pin table contradicts pin plan H
description: docs/15 section 5 lists PIN_RCU_AUX = D4, LEDs D5/D6/D7, buzzer A0 and PIN_SX_NRST = A1 (lines 443-445). The sketch changed in this diff uses PIN_RCU_AUX = 7 (sketch.ino:149), LEDs 4/5/6 and buzzer A1 (sketch.ino:152), and PIN_SX_NRST = A4 (sketch.ino:532), as in D-72. docs/15 was not updated.
failure_scenario: Someone wiring from docs/15 puts the E22 AUX on D4, where the AOS lamp is driven as an output. They also expect the buzzer on A0 and the SX126x reset on A1, where the buzzer actually is.
proposed_fix: Update docs/15 lines 443-445 to RCU D2/D3/D7, LEDs D4/D5/D6, buzzer A1, SX NRST A4, matching sketch.ino and docs/03.
verifier_fix_notes: Update docs/15 section 5 (title UNO Q MCU; DSSQ_RADIO_SX126X row 'RCU on D2 M0, D3 M1, D7 AUX'; PIN_RCU_* D2, D3, D7; lamps D4/D5/D6; buzzer A1; PIN_SX_NRST A4, RXEN A2, TXEN A3). Update docs/03 section 5.1 to pin plan H with the UNO Q MCU pin names in the same change. Record D-71..D-81 in docs/12, which the pending documentation phase (contract section 9) requires anyway.

title: OVERVIEW Frames-tile example uses 2 significant figures; the page shows 3
description: The example reads 'FER 0/344 ≤ 0.87 %'. fpct3() uses toPrecision(3), and 1 - 0.05^(1/344) = 0.867 %, so the tile shows '0.867 %'.
failure_scenario: An operator comparing the page with the documentation sees '0.867 %', not '0.87 %'.
proposed_fix: Change the example to '0/344 ≤ 0.867 %'.
verifier_fix_notes: In docs/13:497, change the example to 'FER 0/344 ≤ 0.867 %'.

title: Link manager reads 'no frame decoded' as FER 0 % and recommends a faster rate
description: evaluate() only checks that the window holds at least MIN_FRAMES RSSI samples (receptions, line 93). A reception is not a decoded frame. When no frame decoded, lm_input() returns fer None, and line 104 (fer = rx.get('fer') or 0.0) turns that into a perfect 0 % FER. The HIGH branch then fires on 'FER < 1 %'. The dashboard (dashboard.html:1668) shows num(rec.frames) with frames = 0 as '0 lost of 0 (0 %)': a FER where nothing was measured.
failure_scenario: SX126x station: every packet calls on_reception, including foreign LoRa packets that are not CADU-length. Sync word 0x12 is a common default, so such packets are plausible at 433 MHz. I reproduced this in review31/LS/lm_nofer.py with 12 foreign packets at -95 dBm, noise -120 dBm, 0 frames. The result is {'action': 'LINKRATE', 'value': 2, 'fer': 0.0, 'frames': 0, 'why': 'margin high: faster rate (predicted 42.0 dB)'}. This can happen in LOS. In AUTO mode the GDS starts a coordinated LINKRATE.
proposed_fix: Return NONE 'insufficient data (< MIN_FRAMES decoded frames in W s)' unless rx['frames'] >= MIN_FRAMES. Never replace fer None with 0.0. In the dashboard, show NA for 'FER in the window' when rec.frames is 0.
verifier_fix_notes: In evaluate(), after the RSSI check, return NONE 'insufficient data (< MIN_FRAMES decoded frames in W s)' when rx.get('frames', 0) < MIN_FRAMES. Keep the RSSI-count check too, and fix its wording to 'receptions'. Do not replace fer None with 0.0: with frames >= MIN_FRAMES, fer is never None. In dashboard.html:1668, use rec.frames > 0 (not num(rec.frames)) before printing a FER. Otherwise show 'n/a (no decoded frame in the window)'.

title: FER colour uses the point estimate, so 0 lost of a few frames is green even when the bound is up to 95 %
description: ferText() sets cls from ci.fer only: green when fer <= 1 %. With zero losses fer is 0, so it is always green, whatever the exact upper bound. The header 'FER 10m', the RECEIVER frame rows and the OVERVIEW 'Frames lost (10 min)' tile all use this class. That contradicts the purpose of the bounds ('a FER from a few frames is not a precise number').
failure_scenario: First frame of a pass: fer_10m_ci = {lost 0, received 1}. The header shows '0/1 ≤ 95.0 %' in green ('ok'). With 0 of 20 frames, the one-sided bound is 13.9 %, above the 10 % 'bad' threshold, and it is still shown green.
proposed_fix: Colour by the one-sided upper bound: bad if one_sided_hi > 0.1, warn if > 0.01, else ok. Or use a neutral class whenever one_sided_hi > 0.01 and lost == 0. Update the docs/13 header and tile colour rules to match.
verifier_fix_notes: Optional improvement. Colour by the evidence instead: when lost == 0 and one_sided_hi > 0.01, use a neutral class (or 'warn' when one_sided_hi > 0.1), with the title 'too few frames to show FER <= 1 %'. Otherwise keep the point-estimate bands. Update the docs/13 4.0 / 3.1 / 4.11 colour rules in the same change.

title: Unsynchronised clock still shows the kernel's saturated maxerror (16 s) as a 'maximum error'
description: When the kernel has no discipline it caps time_maxerror at NTP_PHASE_LIMIT (16,000,000 µs) and sets STA_UNSYNC. That value is a placeholder, not a bound: the real error is unknown. clockRows() (line 2348) and the clockView() tooltip (line 508) still print it as 'Station clock maximum / estimated error 16000 ms / 16000 ms (kernel)'.
failure_scenario: The ground UNO Q boots without network: the kernel returns TIME_ERROR, STA_UNSYNC, maxerror = esterror = 16000000. This machine returned exactly that from query_kernel(). The GDS health panel and the CLOCK tooltip claim a maximum error of 16 s, while the clock may be hours or days off (for example a time restored from the last shutdown).
proposed_fix: Show maxerror and esterror only when ck.synced === true. Otherwise render 'n/a (not synchronised: the kernel gives no bound)'. Document the same in docs/13 13.7.
verifier_fix_notes: Render the error values only when ck.synced === true, in both clockRows and clockView. Otherwise show 'n/a (not synchronised: the kernel gives no bound)'. Optionally do the same in /metrics if maxerror is ever exported (it is not today). Add one sentence to docs/13 13.7: when unsynchronised the kernel reports its 16 s ceiling (NTP_PHASE_LIMIT), which is no bound.

title: Ground RF survey (GSCAN) ranks E22 end-of-range noise octets as the quietest channel
description: D-76 says an E22 noise-register octet at the end of its range, or below -160 dBm, is not a noise power (rxstats.on_noise_octet rejects it). The GSCAN path skips that rule. RadioManager.noise_dbm() returns -(256 - octet), so 0x00 gives -256 dBm. survey() takes min(valid) as 'quietest' (radioctl.py:259-260). The GSCAN job calibrates the values and takes min(allowed) as 'quietest_allowed' (gds.py:1825-1829). The RECEIVER RF-survey bars plot the same values.
failure_scenario: With [gds] rcu = true, run GSCAN while a strong transmitter is on one channel, for example the spacecraft on the bench side by side (record 2026-10-13-A showed 0x00/0xFF octets). That channel reads -256 dBm. The event log reports 'quietest CH<n>, quietest allowed CH<n>' for the busiest channel, and the operator may send LINKCHAN to it.
proposed_fix: In the GSCAN job (E22 only), map each n with rxstats.classify_rssi(n, True) != 'OK' to None before calibration and before both min() calls. Record those channels as 'overload' or 'invalid' in last_scan.
verifier_fix_notes: In the GSCAN job, before calibration, map each n with rxs.classify_rssi(n, not rm.packet) != 'OK' to None (octet radio = E22; on the SX126x only the < -160 dBm INVALID rule applies). Record which channels were rejected (for example res['rejected'] = {ch: 'OVERLOAD'|'INVALID'}). Recompute res['quietest'] from the filtered list, because survey() already picked its min on the raw values, and then 'quietest_allowed'. Better still, apply the classification inside RadioManager.survey() so last_scan is clean for every caller. Draw rejected channels as 'overload' in the bar chart, not as a bar.

title: /metrics exports the link manager's noise-floor upper bound as a plain 'p10 margin'
description: At NOISE_FLOOR, linkmgr.evaluate() stores the upper bound noise_mean - S in recommendation.margin_p10_db (linkmgr.py:103). The page prefixes it with '≤' (dashboard.html:1666). /metrics exports it as dssq_linkmgr_margin_p10_db, 'link manager: p10 margin of its last evaluation', with no state, so a scraper cannot tell a bound from a measurement. With mode OFF, evaluate() returns early and the old recommendation (and gauge) stays exported indefinitely.
failure_scenario: Long-range pass at the noise floor. In the simulator (review31/LS/sim_far.py, RSSI -117, noise -118) the recommendation holds margin_p10_db 7.8 with noise_state NOISE_FLOOR. /metrics shows dssq_linkmgr_margin_p10_db 7.8, a healthy margin above target - 3, while the true margin is unknown and may be negative.
proposed_fix: Export the gauge only when noise_state is SIGNAL or NEAR_NOISE (optionally NOISE_UNKNOWN). Export the bound as dssq_linkmgr_margin_p10_max_db. Clear recommendation when the mode is set to OFF.
verifier_fix_notes: In web.prometheus, export dssq_linkmgr_margin_p10_db only when rec.noise_state is 'SIGNAL' or 'NEAR_NOISE' (optionally NOISE_UNKNOWN). Otherwise export dssq_linkmgr_margin_p10_max_db with the same value. Optionally add a numeric state gauge. In the LINKMGR directive, set self.link_mgr.recommendation = None when the new mode is OFF. Document the split in docs/13 section 16.

title: Uplink noise-floor rule pairs an uplink RSSI from an earlier pass with the current spacecraft noise
description: _budget() applies margin_assessment() to RF uplink_rssi and RF sc_noise_floor. The flight keeps uplink_rssi_ from the last uplink packet indefinitely (flight.cpp:696; never aged or cleared). sc_noise_floor follows the periodic noise queries (flight.cpp:705-711). The two readings can be hours apart, which breaks the same-pass pairing rule (F-P1-5) applied everywhere else. The panel still labels the uplink RSSI and margin 'measured'.
failure_scenario: At AOS the first RF packets arrive before the ground has transmitted in this pass. They carry the previous pass's uplink_rssi (for example -95 dBm at close range) and the current noise. budget.uplink shows 'Received power at the S/C -95 dBm (RF uplink_rssi)', state SIGNAL and a large uplink margin, all describing a different geometry.
proposed_fix: Assess, and show as measured, only when RF cltu_ok or cltu_bad increased since the previous RF packet (an uplink was received in this pass). Otherwise set measured_uplink_rssi_dbm, measured_margin_db and the state to None ('no uplink received this pass').
verifier_fix_notes: In ReceiverStats, remember RF cltu_ok + cltu_bad (uint16; compare modulo 65536) at AOS and on each RF packet. Treat uplink_rssi as 'this pass' only when that sum changed since AOS, because every uplink packet reaching process_tc increments one of them. Otherwise set measured_uplink_rssi_dbm / measured_margin_* to None, with state 'NO_UPLINK_THIS_PASS', and render 'n/a (no uplink received this pass)'. Longer term, add an uplink-RSSI age field to the RF packet (ICD change).

title: Two-way panel shows the spacecraft noise floor unclassified (-256 dBm possible)
description: rx-2way shows fres(tw.sc_noise_floor), the raw RF field. _budget() rejects the same value when classify_rssi() is not OK (rxstats.py:1026-1028), but the dashboard never sees the classified value. A spacecraft E22 noise octet 0x00 or 0xFF, which flight on_noise stores unfiltered, is displayed as a noise floor.
failure_scenario: The spacecraft E22 noise register reads 0x00 (strong signal or bench overload). The UPLINK column shows 'Noise floor -256 dBm'. In the same table the uplink RSSI shows OVERLOAD and the station noise row never contains rejected octets.
proposed_fix: Export the classified value from _budget (budget.uplink.measured_sc_noise_dbm, None when rejected, plus its state) and display that, with 'n/a (end-of-range octet)' when rejected.
verifier_fix_notes: Export the classified value from _budget: budget.uplink.measured_sc_noise_dbm (None when rejected) and measured_sc_noise_state. In the UPLINK column of rx-2way, render that value, or 'n/a (end-of-range octet)' when the state is not OK. Optionally also mark the SPACECRAFT-tab RF sc_noise_floor value.

title: Link budget 'measured received power' is the raw 10-minute RSSI mean, even at the noise floor
description: The _budget docstring says every measured term uses the received power the noise-floor rule accepts, and 'path loss 10-min mean' applies it (ma10). The '= Received power' measured cell is pmres(r10, 'rssi'), the raw 10-minute RSSI mean, and carries a 'measured' badge. At NOISE_FLOOR that number is the noise, placed next to the predicted signal power.
failure_scenario: Simulator at RSSI -117 / noise -118 (review31/LS/sim_far.py): measured_path_loss_mean10m_db is None (rule applied), but '= Received power' shows -117 dBm 'measured'. With a configured distance predicting -135 dBm, the budget suggests the link is 18 dB better than predicted.
proposed_fix: Export ma10['power_dbm'] (for example budget.measured_pr_mean10m_dbm) and show it, with 'n/a (noise floor)' when ma10 is NOISE_FLOOR. Update the docs/13 4.5 row.
verifier_fix_notes: In _budget, export measured_pr_mean10m_dbm = ma10['power_dbm'] and measured_power_state_10m = ma10['state']. In dashboard.html:1448, show that value: noise-removed in NEAR_NOISE, and 'n/a (noise floor)' when ma10 is NOISE_FLOOR. Update the docs/13 4.5 '= Received power' row to match.

title: The ground ignores the Nicla recovery EVR 0x0607, so the Nicla stays LOST and the not-separated alarm clears by itself
description: After a transient Nicla loss the flight never sends a new acquisition report (0x060B). NiclaAru::ok_ is set only in begin() (drivers/payload.cpp:10) and read failures never clear it. The re-probe at flight.cpp:2043 runs only when !aru_.ok(), so probe_nicla()/report_acquired() are not called again. When reads succeed again, start_mag_sample sets SNS_NICLA_ME and FDIR sends only 0x0607 "Nicla Sense ME responding again" (flight.cpp:1996-1998). SensorBusState.on_evr handles 0x0606 as "lost" but has no case for 0x0607, and dictionary.SENSOR_BUS_EVRS does not list it. separation()/counted() count only state == "acquired". docs/13 section 7.6 says the flight reports "when an instrument is lost or found again", and tests/test_sensors.py:225 models the recovery with a 0x060B that the flight never sends on this path.
failure_scenario: I reproduced this with SensorBusState. Boot reports put the Nicla and RM3100 outboard both on A4/A5, plus the 0x060D not-separated WARN: separated is False and the YELLOW reason "sensor wiring: RM3100 and Nicla not on separate buses" is raised. Then the ESLOV bus drops out for more than 6 s: 0x0606 "Nicla Sense ME stopped responding on A4/A5". The Nicla comes back: 0x0607, and HK NICLA_ME is OK again. Result: snapshot nicla.state stays 'lost', the SPACECRAFT row shows red "LOST (EVR 0x0606 ...)", lost = ['Nicla Sense ME (A4/A5)'], separated = None ("unknown (no current acquisition report of the Nicla Sense ME)"). The YELLOW wiring alarm disappears although the two instruments still share A4/A5. This lasts until the next reboot.
proposed_fix: In SensorBusState.on_evr, handle event 0x0607 (text starting "Nicla Sense ME responding again"): if reports['nicla'] exists, call _put('nicla', reports['nicla']['bus'], 'acquired', 0x0607, t, playback) and return True. Add 0x0607 to SENSOR_BUS_EVRS and docs/13 section 7.6. Change test_lost_instruments_and_recovery to use 0x0607. (An alternative is a flight-side report_acquired() on recovery.)
verifier_fix_notes: Ground-only fix (smallest, and it matches the flight as it stands). In SensorBusState.on_evr: if event_id == 0x0607 and text.startswith("Nicla Sense ME responding again") and reports.get('nicla') exists with state 'lost', call _put('nicla', reports['nicla']['bus'], 'acquired', 0x0607, t, playback), increment used, and return True. The flight keeps aru_bus_ unchanged on this path, so the old bus is correct, and the ground recomputes separation itself, so the not-separated verdict and the YELLOW reason come back. Add EVR_NICLA_RECOVERED = 0x0607 with its literal format to SENSOR_BUS_EVRS (the cross-check test compares the formats with the flight). Update docs/13 sections 7.6 and 9.x (state 'acquired' also from 0x0607). Change test_lost_instruments_and_recovery to feed 0x0607 and assert that separated is restored. A flight-side report_acquired() plus report_separation() on recovery is the alternative.

title: IMU_F_PAIRED means different things on the flight and the ground: the flight also requires a valid 9-DOF quaternion
description: The flight sets IMU_F_PAIRED only when aru_imu_paired_ && aru_valid_ && (aru_last_.motion_flags & 1u), i.e. only when q_fus is also valid (flight.cpp:1857). tlm_packets.h:135, docs/05 and the ground all define it as 'q_grv from the same ARU rebuild as q_fus'. The ground requires PAIRED for the linear acceleration and explains a clear PAIRED as 'acc and q_grv not from one ARU rebuild' (sensors.py:222-224). Its own 'paired but ATT b0 QUAT clear' branch (sensors.py:226-227) cannot be reached with real flight data. tests/test_sensors.py:100-102 tests that impossible state.
failure_scenario: The 9-DOF rotation vector is not valid (page 0 b0 clear, e.g. stale or outside the norm gate), while acc (b1) and q_grv come from the same ARU rebuild (imu.seq == r.seq). The flight clears PAIRED. The ground then shows lin_acc as n/a with the false reason "IMU_F_PAIRED clear: acc and q_grv not from one ARU rebuild", although it could compute the value.
proposed_fix: Flight: set IMU_F_PAIRED = aru_imu_paired_ && aru_valid_ (pairing only); the ground already checks ATT b0 QUAT for the heading offset. If the flight is not changed, reword the ground reasons and docs/05 / tlm_packets.h to "not from one ARU rebuild, or no valid 9-DOF rotation vector" and fix the test.
verifier_fix_notes: Preferred: flight.cpp:1857 should set IMU_F_PAIRED when aru_imu_paired_ && aru_valid_ (pairing only). The ground already checks ATT b0 QUAT for the 9-DOF comparison (sensors.py:226). Otherwise keep the flight as it is, redefine PAIRED in tlm_packets.h, docs/05 and docs/13 9.4 as 'same rebuild and a valid q_fus', reword the reasons at sensors.py:223-224 to '... not from one ARU rebuild, or no valid 9-DOF rotation vector', and delete the impossible test case at test_sensors.py:100-102.

title: A saturated imu_nwin (255) is displayed as an exact window count
description: ImuStats::windows() clamps at 255 (attitude.h:104), but the sums keep running over all windows. The ground shows imu_nwin as an exact number, and docs/13:2696 and docs/05 call it the number of 1 s windows in the ATT period without mentioning saturation. ATT periods longer than 255 s are realistic: PKTRATE ATT accepts up to 3600 s; the on-board stretch at ultra-long-range settings gives CRUISE 60 s x 4.74 = 284 s at SX126x profile 0 (R3 section 5.8); and ImuStats is not reset while ATT is off in SAFE, so the first ATT after SAFE covers the whole SAFE period. The simulator (sim.py _imu_stats) aggregates only the newest 255 windows, unlike the flight.
failure_scenario: After PKTRATE ATT 600 (or CRUISE at SX126x p0, or the first ATT after an hour in SAFE), the SCIENCE IMU table reads "Windows aggregated 255", while vib_rms / rate_mean / peaks cover 600 or more windows.
proposed_fix: When nwin == 255, show ">= 255 (counter saturated)". State the saturation in docs/05 (imu_nwin) and docs/13 section 9.4. In the simulator, aggregate all windows and report only the count as min(n, 255).
verifier_fix_notes: Dashboard: when nwin == 255, show '>= 255 (counter saturated; the statistics cover the whole period)'. Optionally expose imu.nwin_saturated from sensors.py. State the saturation in docs/05 (imu_nwin) and docs/13 9.4. Simulator: aggregate every window since imu_win_end and send imu_nwin = min(n, 255). If the cost matters, cap the work, but compute rate_mean, vib_rms and peaks over the full set the way the flight does.

title: The noise floor shown for |omega| of the MEAN rate is the single-sample noise
description: RATE_FLOOR_DPS = 0.07 x sqrt(3) = 0.121 deg/s is the |omega| noise of one gyro sample. The dashboard shows it next to "|omega| of the mean rate" (dashboard.html:2077), and the spin-axis n/a reason (sensors.py:254-255) and docs/13:2699 also use it. rate_mean is the mean of 20-25 samples per window (ARU close_window) and then the mean of nwin windows. With independent samples its white-noise floor is 0.121/sqrt(25*nwin): 0.024 deg/s for one window, 0.0086 deg/s for 8 windows. So the displayed 'floor' is 5-14x too high. It is also not the real limit, which is the unspecified residual gyro offset (+/-1 deg/s with fast offset compensation off).
failure_scenario: TEST mode, 8 windows, body at rest. The table says "|omega| 0.05 deg/s (noise floor est. 0.12 deg/s)", which suggests the reading is below the noise. The averaging floor is about 0.009 deg/s, and the value that actually limits the reading (the residual offset) is not stated at all.
proposed_fix: Either compute and show the floor of the mean as RATE_FLOOR_DPS/sqrt(25*nwin), labelled as an estimate, or relabel the value as "single-sample |omega| noise". In both cases, state next to it that the residual gyro offset (not specified) limits |omega_mean|. Update docs/13 section 9.4 to match.
verifier_fix_notes: Relabel instead of recomputing. In the dashboard and docs/13 9.4, call RATE_FLOOR_DPS 'single-sample |omega| noise est. 0.12 deg/s; the mean is limited by the unspecified residual gyro offset (T-SC-14)'. Reword the spin n/a reason to '... 10 x the 0.12 deg/s single-sample noise est.'. Leave SPIN_AXIS_FACTOR unchanged. If a white-noise floor of the mean is wanted as well, show RATE_FLOOR_DPS/sqrt(25*nwin) separately, labelled as an estimate.

title: "stationary" is reported for the whole ATT period even when windows were missed (IMU_F_GAP)
description: motion_state() decides from the windows the flight happened to read. The flight reads page 2 only in its 1 Hz sample, and that sample is deferred while the transmitter is keyed (flight.cpp:2234 `if (tx_state_ != TX_IDLE) return;`). At 2.4 kbit/s (busy 1267 ms, frame period >= 2.5 s at the 50 % duty limit), 1 s windows regularly go unread, so IMU_F_GAP is set in most TEST periods. The motion row and docs/13:2702 still present the verdict as the state of the whole ATT period.
failure_scenario: In TEST mode the body moves during windows the flight did not read (they fell inside transmission bursts). The windows it did read are quiet: rate_peak 0.3 deg/s, vib_peak 7 mg. The panel says "stationary" for the period, while the GAP badge sits in another row.
proposed_fix: When GAP is set, qualify the verdict, e.g. "stationary in the N windows seen (windows missed)", or return "unknown" with a reason in na['motion']. Document this in docs/13 section 9.4.
verifier_fix_notes: When imu.gap is set, qualify a 'stationary' verdict on the ground. Add na-style text, or a motion_note such as 'stationary in the <nwin> windows read (windows missed: a short motion between them is not seen)', in sensors.py and render it in the Motion state row. Document this in docs/13 9.4. Do not change the verdict logic itself.

title: The simulator sets IMU_F_STATS with imu_nwin = 0
description: _att always sends imu_flags = IMU_FLAGS_SIM = 0x47, which includes STATS (b1). When _imu_stats finds no completed window it returns {'imu_nwin': 0}. The flight sets STATS exactly when windows() != 0 (flight.cpp:1863), so the simulator sends a combination the flight never produces.
failure_scenario: First ATT after simulator start or a software reset (SCLK < 1 s), or two ATTs within one SCLK second: STATS is set while imu_nwin is 0 and the statistics are sentinels. The ground copes with it, so this is not caught.
proposed_fix: When imu_nwin == 0, send IMU_FLAGS_SIM & ~0x02.
verifier_fix_notes: In SimSpacecraft._att: stats = self._imu_stats(t); v['imu_flags'] = IMU_FLAGS_SIM if stats.get('imu_nwin') else IMU_FLAGS_SIM & ~0x02. Optionally add a test that STATS == (imu_nwin != 0).

title: docs/05 EVR table leaves out the 0x060D "not separated" WARN text
description: evrs() keeps only the first format per event id (rows.setdefault). 0x060D has two flight formats: the wrong-bus WARN and "%s and %s both on %s: not separated (docs/03)" (flight.cpp:550). docs/05 line 623 lists only the first, so the WARN behind the YELLOW alarm "sensor wiring: RM3100 and Nicla not on separate buses" is missing from the EVR reference.
failure_scenario: An operator looks up the EVR text "... both on A4/A5: not separated (docs/03)" in docs/05 and does not find it.
proposed_fix: Collect every distinct format per id (e.g. dict[str, list]) and print one row per format; regenerate docs/05.
verifier_fix_notes: In evrs(), collect dict[str, list[tuple[sev, fmt]]], append each distinct (sev, fmt), and print one row per format (repeating the id). Then regenerate docs/05. The same change also covers any other id with more than one format.

title: The sigma multiples given for still_rate_dps / still_vib_mg are wrong
description: docs/15:366-367 call the thresholds about 3 sigma (rate) and about 3.5 sigma (vibration) of the three-axis datasheet noise, and docs/13:2702 says 'about 3 sigma'. With the same docs' noise values (0.07 deg/s and 1.2 mg per axis, i.e. 0.121 deg/s and 2.08 mg over three axes), 0.5 deg/s is 4.1 sigma and 10 mg is 4.8 sigma. The 3 sigma / 3.5 sigma values would be 0.36 deg/s and 7.3 mg (R3 section 5.9).
failure_scenario: An operator tuning the thresholds from the docs sets still_rate_dps = 0.36 ('3 sigma'). The peak of 200 or more samples of a 3-D Gaussian magnitude at rest reaches about 3.6-4.2 sigma, so a body at rest is flagged as moving.
proposed_fix: Write "about 4 sigma (0.5 / 0.121)" and "about 5 sigma (10 / 2.08)", and note that a peak over many samples needs that margin.
verifier_fix_notes: Correct the text in docs/15 and docs/13 9.4: 'about 4 sigma (0.5 / 0.121)' and 'about 5 sigma (10 / 2.08) of the three-axis datasheet noise, margin for the peak over many samples and the unspecified 25 Hz noise, VERIFY T-SC-14'. No code change.

title: The 'older ATT without the 6-DOF part' case cannot come out of the GDS
description: imu_products has a path for an ATT without imu_flags ("imu_flags missing: no 6-DOF part in this ATT"), and test_sentinels_give_reasons_never_numbers tests it with a hand-made dict. The Decommutator rejects a 37-octet ATT v3 ("ATT: 37 octets of user data, the layout has 59"), so the whole packet is dropped as a decom error, including its v3 attitude fields.
failure_scenario: A 3.1 ground with a 3.0 flight: every ATT gives a DECOM WARN, the Attitude panel shows 'no ATT packet yet', and the IMU panel says "no ATT packet yet" instead of the tested reason. The test passes but does not cover the real behaviour.
proposed_fix: Either decode a v3-length ATT as the 37-octet prefix (fields 0-36 present, 6-DOF absent) so the documented reason appears, or remove the unreachable branch and the test claim.
verifier_fix_notes: Simplest: remove the claim from the test comment, or keep the branch as defensive code and rename the test comment to 'a dict without imu_flags (defensive; the Decommutator rejects a v3-length ATT)'. Decode the 37-octet prefix only if mixed 3.0/3.1 operation is a requirement. It is not one now.

title: The docs understate the simulator's tumble rate
description: docs/13 says the simulator tumbles at 5-8 deg/s. For the _rot tumble, |omega|^2 = psi'^2 + theta'^2 + phi'^2 - 2 psi' phi' sin(theta), which gives 5.4 to 10.1 deg/s. The simulated ATT shows rate_peak up to 10.3 deg/s.
failure_scenario: A reader checking the simulator example finds |omega| and peak values above 8 deg/s and suspects an error.
proposed_fix: Change the text to "5-10 deg/s".
verifier_fix_notes: Change docs/13:2722 to 'about 5-10 deg/s'.

title: The game rotation vector row says 'as sent' but shows the normalised quaternion
description: imu.q_grv is unit_quat(), i.e. divided by its norm (sensors.py:118-119). The flight gate lets norms of 0.9-1.1 through. The row label says "(device->GRV world, as sent)", while docs/13:2688 correctly says 'normalised'.
failure_scenario: An ARU sends q_grv with norm 1.05 (inside the gate). The table shows components about 5 % smaller than the telemetry under a label that says 'as sent'.
proposed_fix: Relabel the row "(device->GRV world, normalised)".
verifier_fix_notes: Relabel the row 'Quaternion w x y z (device→GRV world, scalar first, normalised)'. No code change.
